title: Upgrade dry-run telemetry assertions and probe list for VPC/on-prem
body:
Purpose and scope:
This note is a pragmatic dry-run checklist and telemetry assertion set for VPC/on-prem private deployments ahead of major runtime or TF module upgrades. Use in staging or mirror environments to validate behavior before production rollout. Focus: measurable telemetry, short smoke probes, and a compact terraform troubleshooting cheat-sheet.

Assumptions:
- You have a staging VPC or an air-gapped mirror that closely matches prod networking and GPU topology.
- Terraform state is accessible and you have an admin TF token.
- K8s cluster name, namespace (default: redwood), and kubeconfig are ready.

High-level dry-run flow (30–120m):
1) Baseline capture (10–30m): collect current metrics and logs to compare after the dry-run.
2) TF dry-run: terraform init/plan with -out and review diffs. No apply in prod.
3) Apply to mirror: limited apply to a sandbox cluster, run smoke probes.
4) Telemetry assertions: validate threshold checks.
5) Rollback and artifact collection: snapshot state and logs.

Baseline capture commands (minimum):
- kubectl -n redwood get pods -o wide > baseline_pods.txt
- kubectl -n redwood top pods --containers > baseline_top.txt || use metrics-server
- nvidia-smi --query-gpu=utilization.gpu,temperature.gpu --format=csv -l 1 > baseline_gpu.log (15s sample)
- curl -sS -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" https://<gateway>/healthz > baseline_health.txt
- curl -w "time_total:%{time_total}\n" -o /dev/null -s https://<gateway>/v1/generate?model=small > baseline_latency.txt

Terraform dry-run notes and commands:
- Run with explicit provider versions: terraform init -upgrade -backend-config="bucket=redwood-tf-state"
- Use plan output for exact diffs: terraform plan -out=upgrade.plan -var-file=staging.tfvars
- Inspect changes that cause replacements ("-/+" and "replace") carefully for resources with storage or IPs.
- Common traps: provider version drift, module input type change, network MTU or route overlaps, tainted resources, missing resource import.
- Useful commands: terraform show upgrade.plan > upgrade-plan.txt; TF_LOG=DEBUG terraform apply -parallelism=10 -auto-approve (only in sandbox)
- If resource needs import: terraform import module.foo.aws_eip.this <id>

Telemetry assertions (automatable checks):
- Scheduling and capacity:
  - pod_pending_count == 0 (baseline) -> allow <=1 transient; >3 sustained for 5m FAIL
  - node_unschedulable increase == 0; if nodes cordoned, require annotation in run notes
- Runtime reliability:
  - container_restart_rate (per pod) <= 1 restart / 60m
  - OOMKilled events increment == 0
- Latency and throughput:
  - p95 inference latency <= 1.5x baseline p95 for identical request set in 10m window
  - p99 inference latency <= 2.5x baseline p99 (investigate if exceeded)
  - tokens/sec >= 80% of baseline during steady load probe (30s sampling)
- Resource utilization:
  - GPU utilization should not spike > 1.4x baseline for a sustained 60s unless expected by config changes
  - KV cache hit rate (if instrumented) >= baseline - 10%
- Errors and logs:
  - new occurrences of these log fingerprints are FAIL: 
    - "OOMKilled"
    - "failed to bind"
    - "TLS handshake failed"
    - "permission denied" with runtime socket or /dev/nvidia*
    - "failed to allocate memory for attention key"
  - Increase in ERROR/CRITICAL log lines > 10% over baseline -> investigate

Smoke probes (runnable small scripts):
- Health probe: curl /healthz (expect 200, response time < 200ms)
- Inference sample: send 3 small generate requests (same prompt) and assert identical status and <= configured latency thresholds
- Streaming probe: open a streaming session for 30s and ensure bytes flow continuously (no early EOF)
- Prefix-cache probe: send increasing prompt lengths to measure cold vs warm latency; expect warm latency <= cold * 0.6 on cached models
- Embedding probe: run embeddings for 10 documents and compare dimensionality and response time
- Rollback probe: send a synthetic high-QPS burst (10 rps for 30s) to confirm autoscaling policy and throttling behavior

Typical failure fingerprints and immediate remediation hints:
- "ImagePullBackOff" -> check registry auth, network egress, and image tag in TF plan. Retry pull on node; kubectl describe pod shows events.
- OOMKilled on model container -> lower batch size, check cgroup driver mismatch, examine container memory limit. If new after upgrade, revert to prior image.
- Pod scheduling stuck -> inspect pod tolerations, taints, available node allocatable resources, and network routes. Often a changed nodeSelector or wrong label in TF module.
- IP conflict / route missing -> verify VPC subnets and MTU. Check host route tables and firewall rules.
- Kubelet kernel errors or GPU driver absent -> check dmesg and nvidia-smi, verify driver/package versions.

Quick remediation sequence (sandbox-first):
1) If catastrophic: cordon problematic node(s): kubectl cordon <node> and drain if safe.
2) Scale down replica counts or set TrafficWeight=0 for new variant if using rollout config.
3) Reapply previous TF state: terraform apply -state=backup.tfstate (only after review).
4) Restart sequence: restart runtime pods in order: control plane -> workers. Use kubectl rollout restart deployment/runtime-control -n redwood then rollout restart ds/runtime-worker -n redwood.

What to collect for support (attach to ticket):
- upgrade-plan.txt (terraform show output)
- tfstate snapshot (state pull)
- kube logs: kubectl -n redwood logs <pod> --previous (if restart happened)
- dmesg, journalctl -u kubelet, nvidia-smi output
- metrics dump for the 10m window around the test (prometheus query result)
- a concise reproduction script if applicable (curl requests or small client)

Post-dry-run acceptance criteria (pass to schedule prod upgrade):
- No increase in critical errors; container restart rate and OOM events within baseline tolerance.
- p95 latency within 1.5x baseline for test workload; tokens/sec >= 80% of baseline.
- TF plan shows no destructive replacements for stateful resources without documented mitigation.
- Runbook and rollback steps validated and time-to-rollback < 30m in sandbox.

Appendix: short TF debugging snippets:
- Show planned replacements with reason:
  terraform plan -out=plan.out && terraform show -json plan.out | jq '.resource_changes[] | {address,change: .change.actions}'
- Force taint to test create-path: terraform taint module.runtime.aws_instance.worker[0]
- Extract provider versions: terraform providers lock -platform=linux_amd64 && cat .terraform.lock.hcl

Notes and open questions:
- We still need a small harness to automate the telemetry assertions above (prometheus queries + pass/fail).
- Investigate adding a dedicated "dry-run" TF workspace with read-only access to prod state for safer diffs.

If you run this and hit a pattern not documented here, add the fingerprint and quick remediation to this doc (notes field).
